To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Leucine supplementation does not prevent muscle loss and muscle strength loss during short term immobilization in young healthy men.
Leucine supplementation did not prevent the loss in muscle mass and strength that occurs during a short-term immobilization intervention.
leucine supplementation did not prevent muscle loss in the immobilized leg.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of short-term immobilization of a limb on skeletal muscle and its metabolic properties.
the role of the immune system in muscle loss and muscle loss prevention.
the effects of leucine supplementation on muscle mass and function during a period of disuse in healthy young adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a daily leucine intake of 7.5 g, with each meal, does not attenuate muscle loss in healthy young men during 7 days of unilateral leg immobilization.
the present data do not support a role of leucine in the regulation of muscle protein synthesis and breakdown in vivo.
the supplementation of 7.5 g of leucine daily during a 7-day period of limb immobilization did not affect the decline of leg muscle mass or strength in healthy, young men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leucine supplementation is ineffective in attenuating muscle loss during a short period (one week) of disuse.
leucine supplementation does not have an anabolic effect on the skeletal muscle during short periods of inactivity in young, healthy men.
leucine supplementation does not prevent muscle loss during disuse in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leucine supplementation is not a magic bullet to maintain muscle mass during a short period (1 week) of physical inactivity in healthy, young men.
the maintenance of skeletal muscle during brief periods of physical inactivation is a complex process that requires more than just the provision of a single essential amino acid.
leucine supplementation does not attenuate muscle loss during short-term immobilization.
